Georgina Energy plc
("Georgina", "Georgina Energy" or the "Company")
Hussar EP513 Prospect Update
Georgina Energy Plc, (LSE: GEX.L), a helium, hydrogen and natural gas exploration and development company with strategic permits in Australia, confirms that civil engineering contractors have completed all pre-drill site and road access works to enable the contracted Ensign 970 drill rig to test of this exciting prospect, which has 330 km² of areal closure and is one of the largest subsalt helium, hydrogen and hydrocarbons prospects remaining untested in onshore Australia.
Highlights
The drilling pad, water well, Turkey’s nest and sump are completed and lined with waterproof sheeting.
The water well has been completed and tested on a long term test delivering some 260,000 litres per day.
The 20 inch conductor pipe has been drilled and cemented in place.
The Hussar airstrip has been cleared, gravelled and rolled to provide a 1,400m length airstrip capable of operation in virtually any weather.
Access roads have been cleared, graded and gravelled and compacted where necessary.
Mobilisation planning with the Ensign Rig 970 has been almost completed.
Delays for Drill program
The civil engineers and water well drillers have begun demobilising from site however there has been unseasonal record-breaking rain in the district which has prevented all of the contractors’ equipment and trucks being able to demobilise. The Company remained optimistic along with Ensign that mobilisation would occur in September as planned but the continuing road closures have further complicated the program along with flooding.
Leonora, a town close to the start of the main access road recorded a record-breaking 58.8mm of rain in the 24 hours to 9:00 am on Monday, September 7, 2026. This resulted in:
The wettest September day on record for a month that typically averages less than 10mm.
The heaviest spring daily rainfall ever recorded in Leonora.
The wettest day overall in nine years, delivering over a quarter of the town's average annual rainfall in just one day.
The second-wettest September on record for the town overall in 129 years of data collection.
Ongoing road closures in within the Wiluna Shire Council:
www.wiluna.wa.gov.au
Ongoing restrictions on heavy vehicle access (RAV-Restricted Access Vehicles):
www.wiluna.wa.gov.au
have prevented any movement of overwidth, over length or over weight vehicles at any times when roads are wet. This means that prime movers hauling triple trailers are banned from large sections of the road network to Hussar within the Shire.
The Company have held ongoing discussions with Ensign Drilling and both parties have concluded that the mobilisation of the drilling rig to the Hussar site represents an extraordinarily high chance of being halted “en route” currently. Furthermore, the Company risks incurring material standby charges from not only Ensign but the other service contractors necessarily involved in this operation which would make any continuing delays costly especially as such time delays cannot be reliably forecast in the current circumstances.
The Company is hopeful of mobilising the drilling rig and associated service contractors in a timely fashion subject to safety constraints including the weather and road conditions to allow for the safe mobilisation of the equipment and personnel.
Further updates will follow as we progress towards a revised spud date with additional site photos which can be viewed by shareholders on the Georgina website.
Anthony Hamilton, Chief Executive Officer of Georgina Energy, commented:
“Georgina’s contractors have done an excellent job of preparing the site and access roads to enable the mobilisation of the Ensign 970 drill rig to enable the drill testing of this exciting prospect, however, unexpected heavy rainfall and road closures have caused the targeted drill program to be delayed and we look forward to making further announcements in due course.”

Georgina Energy has two principal onshore interests held through its wholly owned Australian subsidiary, Westmarket O&G.
The first, the Hussar Prospect is located in the Officer Basin in Western Australia and Westmarket O&G holds a 100% working interest in the exploration permit.

latest.content:

Georgina Energy PLC

THIS ANNOUNCEMENT RELATES TO THE
DISCLOSURE
OF INFORMATION THAT QUALIFIED OR MAY HAVE QUALIFIED AS INSIDE INFORMATION WITHIN THE MEANING OF (A) ARTICLE 7(1) OF UK MAR IN SO FAR AS IT RELATES TO ORDINARY SHARES ISSUED BY GEORGINA ENERGY PLC
Georgina Energy plc
("Georgina", "Georgina Energy" or the "Company")
Hussar EP513 Pre-drilling Civil Engineering Update
Georgina Energy Plc, (LSE: GEX.L), a helium, hydrogen and natural gas exploration and development company with strategic permits in Australia, confirms that civil engineering contractors on site at the Hussar prospect have completed setting the 20-inch conductor pipe, as well as the required water well and remedial upgrades to the Hussar airstrip. These works, including already completed site and camp pad preparation, represent another key step forward in advancing the planned drilling programme at the Hussar prospect.
Highlights
The twenty inch conductor pipe has been set and will be cemented in the 26-inch hole opening.
The water well drill rig has completed the water well drilling with a consistent flow rate.
Gravelling, rolling and compacting of the drilling and camp pads has been completed.
The Hussar airstrip has been extended for Medevac and crew changes and has been completely rolled, compacted and a low spot prone to waterlogging has been gravelled and compacted.
Gravel has been carted to the main access road and laying and compacting of several low spots prone to flooding has commenced.
All the pre-drilling site works are expected to be completed shortly.
With 330 km² of areal closure at 3U level, the Hussar prospect ranks among the largest subsalt helium, hydrogen and hydrocarbon prospects onshore Australia that remains untested. The Hussar prospect has an Independent Geological Report dated 1
st
February 2026 by Competent Person, Mr Maki Petkovski, certifying unrisked SPE PRMS (the Society of Petroleum Engineers and Petroleum Resource Management Systems) net attributable 2U Prospective Resources of 283 BCF helium, 315 BCF hydrogen and 2.93 TCF of hydrocarbon gas.
Based on the pricing of Helium US$450/MCFG and Hydrogen US$2.65/kg and US$8/MCF for hydrocarbon gas, these volumes would equate to a total potential combined net attributable unrisked potential in-situ value of c.
US$152 billion.
Note:
These are estimated “in-situ” values from the AER (Australian Energy Regulator) and HNT (Helium Price Index) developed by the Company based on unrisked 2U SPE PRMS (Society of Petroleum Engineers Petroleum Resources Management) Prospective (recoverable) Resources; they exclude production, separation and transport-to-market costs, and there is no certainty that all or any part of these Prospective Recoverable Resources will be commercially recovered.
Running the 20-inch conductor into the 26-inch open hole
Aerial view of the drilling site prior to running in the 20-inch conductor pipe.
Aerial view of the extended Hussar Airstrip – 1,400m in length.
The Hussar EP513 prospect re-entry in Exploration Permit 513 in the Officer Basin in Western Australia is primarily targeting subsalt reservoir formations, including the Townsend Formation and fractured Neoproterozoic basement lithologies, for helium, hydrogen and natural gas and is planned to drill to a Total Depth of approximately 3,200m which may be extended depending on gas occurrences and reservoir quality. Globally, fractured basement reservoirs similar to that targeted in the Hussar Prospect, have proven to be prolific producers. The Bach Ho field in fractured basement offshore Vietnam for example, at its peak produced 1.6 BCFGE (billion cubic feet of gas equivalent) per day and has been in continuous production for over 40 years. (
https://www.saltworkconsultants.com/downloads/Bach_Ho_Cuong_Warren_09.pdf
)
A secondary target is the hydrocarbon gas potential in the Kanpa and Hussar formations overlying the primary subsalt targets. These formations have not been adequately tested to date but have shown excellent porosities and hydrocarbon shows during previous drilling.
Further updates will follow as we progress towards
spud date along with additional site photos which can be viewed by shareholders on the Company’s website.
Anthony Hamilton, Chief Executive Officer of Georgina Energy, commented:
“Completion of these civil engineering works is crucial to our planned drilling operation; the operation requires a reliable and significant water supply which we now have in place and the setting of the 20” conductor will save a lot of time once the Ensign Rig 970 has arrived on site.
This represents another important achievement in the necessary works to expedite mobilisation of the
Ensign 970 drill rig to drill test this exciting prospect
.”

Completion of £1.25 Million Fundraise
Georgina Energy plc (LSE: GEX), is pleased to announce that it has successfully raised £1.25m through the issue of 10,000,000 new ordinary shares at a placing price of 12.5 pence per share (the "Placing"). The Company will issue investors with one warrant per one placing share at an exercise price of 14 pence expiring 5 years from Admission ("Investor Warrants").
Use of Proceeds
The net proceeds of the Placing will be used to advance Mount Winter and for general working capital.
Broker Warrants
The Company will issue 600,000 Broker Warrants exercisable at 12 pence and expire five years from the date of Admission.
Admission of Placing Shares
An application has been made for
10,000,000
new ordinary shares to be admitted to trading on the official list and main market of the London Stock Exchange from 8.00 a.m. on 2 September 2026 ("Admission").
Total Voting Rights
In accordance with the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules, the Company confirms that following Admission, the Company's enlarged issued ordinary share capital will comprise 280,861,707 Ordinary Shares. The Company does not hold any Ordinary Shares in Treasury. Therefore, following Admission, the above figure may be used by shareholders in the Company as the denominator for the calculations to determine if they are required to notify their interest in, or a change to their interest in the Company, under the FCA's Disclosure Guidance and Transparency Rules.

Hussar EP513 Water Well Completed
Georgina Energy Plc, (LSE: GEX.L), a helium, hydrogen and natural gas exploration and development company with strategic permits in Australia, confirms that civil engineering contractors on site have completed the required water well and will soon be commencing setting the conductor pipe for programmed Q3 Hussar drilling program. These works, including site and camp preparation, represent another key step forward in mobilisation of the contracted Ensign 970 drill rig to site.
Highlights
·
The spud date in September 2026 remains on target.
·
The water well has been completed with a consistent flow rate of between 250,000 to 350,000 litres per day for the rig water supply. This will be used for drilling fluid makeup water with a proportion being purified with Reverse Osmosis treatment for ablutions and cooking.
·
The water well drill rig will now move closer to the centre of the drilling pad and drill and set the 20 inch conductor pipe before the Ensign Rig 970 arrives on site.
·
The civil engineers have advanced site works including excavation of the Turkey's Nest (a water storage pond) and the sump to contain drill cuttings and any excess drilling fluid. The waterproof linings have also been completed.
·
Rolling and compacting of the drilling and camp pads has also commenced.
·
Site grading and trimming have been completed.
·
Gravel has been delivered and graded at the camp pad, with further gravel carted to the road and graded. Additional gravel supplies are also in place.
With over 300 km² of areal closure, the Hussar prospect ranks among the largest subsalt helium, hydrogen and hydrocarbon prospects onshore Australia that remains untested.

company_30s.what_they_do: Hussar Energy (ticker GEX.L) is a small, early‑stage oil & gas exploration firm focused on drilling and developing a single offshore well (EP513).  The company’s core activity is to secure and drill a water well, build a production facility, and bring the asset into first‑time production.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The firm operates in a niche segment of the UK offshore market, targeting a 3‑4 km offshore field that could supply the UK’s growing domestic energy demand.  Its success would give it a foothold in a sector with limited competition and a clear path to revenue generation once the well is operational.
company_30s.current_state: GEX.L is in a pre‑production, cash‑burning phase.  Recent funding of £1.25 million and ongoing drilling work suggest the company is keeping its operations alive while it waits for the first production run.  The stock trades well below its all‑time high, reflecting the heavy capital expenditure and uncertain commodity outlook.

rns_narrative: The company has just closed a £1.25 million raise and is actively drilling the EP513 water well.  The latest site‑works update confirms that the drilling rig is on schedule and that the water well is complete, a key milestone that brings the project closer to first production.
Corporate governance moves – share awards and warrant exercises – indicate management is aligning incentives with shareholders, while the AGM results show a stable, if modest, shareholder base.
Together these events paint a picture of a company that is surviving the cash‑burn cycle and is now poised to transition from construction to production.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quiet optimism – the community is largely silent but a small, informed group is cautiously hopeful.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls argue that the completion of the water well and the recent funding round give the firm a clear path to first production, which could lift the share price sharply.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears point to the high capital requirements, the risk of drilling delays, and the uncertain price of oil and gas as reasons to stay away.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The community’s mood has shifted from neutral to mildly bullish after the fundraise, but overall engagement remains low.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for GEX.L is flat – no public interest, which is a green flag for a contrarian play.

near_term_catalysts: Official announcement of drilling completion and first production data.
Positive well‑testing results that demonstrate commercial viability.
A subsequent funding round or a strategic partnership that reduces the capital burden.
An upward swing in oil or gas prices that improves the project’s economics.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a sharp volume spike coupled with a breakout above the current support level (roughly 14% of the all‑time high).  A clear, positive news release from the drilling team or a financing announcement would confirm the mean‑reversion thesis.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock sits in the early‑stage of a deep‑crash recovery.  Capitulation appears complete, and the APEX score indicates tight compression – the classic setup for a contrarian bounce once a catalyst arrives.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: The share sits roughly 86 % below its peak, so a move to the halfway point would generate a ~200 % return.  Historical green‑signal data shows a 39 % average return and 40 % win rate, meaning the upside is well‑documented.  The mean‑reversion thesis is clear: once the well is proven, the market will re‑price the company toward its intrinsic value.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The main risks are drilling delays, cost overruns, and a weak commodity market.  If the well fails or production is delayed beyond the next quarter, the share could stay at or near its current level, delivering a modest 14 % return (the current price relative to the all‑time high).
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Risk: 14 % of the all‑time high (the current price).  Reward: ~200 % to the halfway point.  Ratio: roughly 1 : 14 – a highly asymmetrical play.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter after a confirmed volume surge and the price holds above the 14 % support level.  Allocate 5 % of available capital per position.  Place a stop 10 % below the support to protect against a false breakout.
playbook.if_watching: Hold off until the company announces drilling completion or first‑time production data.  A news release that confirms commercial viability would be the trigger.
playbook.if_passing: None identified – no delisting, bankruptcy, or fraud risk.

ai_insights.bottom_line: Deep crash, imminent drilling completion and a clear path to first production give this contrarian play a high upside with a modest downside – a classic asymmetric bet.
